extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and parties requesting/defending ex parte reexamination
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for deciding whether to order ex parte reexamination under 35 U.S.C. 302/303, including the criteria for a "substantial new question of patentability," handling of second/subsequent requests, claim scope considerations, timing, and processing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial New Question of Patentability (SNQ)
rubrics_metrics.description: The presence or absence of “a substantial new question of patentability” determines whether or not reexamination is ordered; the term is not defined in the statute and must be developed case-by-case using case law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A prior art patent or printed publication raises an SNQ where there is a substantial likelihood that a reasonable examiner would consider the prior art important in deciding patentability. It is sufficient that an SNQ exists as to at least one claim. The same question of patentability is not an SNQ if it has been (A) decided in a final holding of invalidity by a federal court (after all appeals), (B) decided in an earlier concluded examination or review by the Office, or (C) raised to or by the Office in a pending reexamination or supplemental examination. It is not necessary that a prima facie case of unpatentability exist; an SNQ can exist even if the examiner would not necessarily reject the claim as fully anticipated or obvious. See In re Etter and related citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior Art Basis for SNQ
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination whether an SNQ exists can be based upon any prior art patents or printed publications, not just the art cited in the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner may base the determination on: (a) the patents/publications relied on in the request, (b) a combination of those and other prior art found elsewhere, or (c) entirely different patents/printed publications. The examiner may perform a limited search to supply deficiencies in the prior art cited in the request where there is a reasonable likelihood additional prior art can be found to supply the deficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Old Art (previously cited/considered) May Serve as Sole Basis
rubrics_metrics.description: For reexamination ordered on or after November 2, 2002, reliance on previously cited/considered art ("old art") does not necessarily preclude the existence of an SNQ based solely on that old art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determinations where old art is used as the sole basis require a fact-specific inquiry; old art may constitute an SNQ if it is presented/viewed in a new light or in a different way (e.g., in view of a material new argument or claim scope interpretation). When using old art solely, include form paragraph 22.01.01 in the order and explain how the old art is being presented in a new light. The form paragraph explains bracket insertions and must be used only the first time the already-cited art is applied in the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to Set Forth Pertinency and Manner for Each Claim
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 302 requires that the request must set forth the pertinency and manner of applying cited prior art to every claim for which reexamination is requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the requester fails to apply the art to certain claims, requester is not statutorily entitled to reexamination of those claims. Failure to set forth pertinency and manner as required by 37 CFR 1.510(b) will generally result in that claim not being reexamined and may result in no filing date being awarded to the request. See MPEP §§ 2217 and 2227.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims Considered in Decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims of the patent in effect at the time of the determination are the basis for deciding whether an SNQ is present (37 CFR 1.515(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office’s determination will generally be limited to the claims for which reexamination was requested, but the examiner is not strictly limited and can base an SNQ on other claims of the patent. If the requester wanted all claims reexamined, they should have included them. The Office may also initiate reexamination on non-requested claims under 35 U.S.C. 303(a). Amendments/new claims in copending reexamination or reissue proceedings will not be considered when deciding the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for Deciding Request
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination of whether or not to reexamine must be made within 3 months following the filing date of a request (35 U.S.C. 303(a) and 37 CFR 1.515(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the 3-month period ends on a Saturday, Sunday, or federal holiday in D.C., the determination must be mailed by the preceding business day. A determination to reexamine may be made at any time during the enforceability of the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second or Subsequent Request Must Present a Different SNQ
rubrics_metrics.description: If a second or subsequent request is filed while a first ex parte reexamination is pending, the second/subsequent request is evaluated based on whether it raises a substantial new question of patentability different from that raised in the pending reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the second request includes prior art that raised the SNQ in the pending reexamination, it should be denied. If it raises a different SNQ as to some claims but not others, it may be granted in part. The decision is based on the claims in effect at the time of determination (37 CFR 1.515(a)). A second/subsequent request may also provide information directed to proposed new or amended claims in the pending reexamination, but to be granted it must independently provide a different SNQ for the existing claims in effect at the time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial Grant Possibility for Subsequent Requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a subsequent request raises a different SNQ as to some patent claims but not others, the request may be granted in part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples cited include orders in specific reexamination control numbers. Examiner should grant reexamination only for claims where a different SNQ is presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harassment Filings and Suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If a second or subsequent request appears filed for purposes of harassment, the patent owner may file a petition under 37 CFR 1.182; if granted, prosecution on that second/subsequent reexamination can be suspended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merger of such a request with pending proceedings can unduly prolong matters and is inconsistent with the requirement that reexamination proceedings be conducted with special dispatch. Use 37 CFR 1.182 petition procedures to address harassment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Prior Favorable Office Decisions on Same Art
rubrics_metrics.description: An SNQ is not raised by prior art presented in a request if the Office has previously considered the same question of patentability as to the claim and reached a favorable decision for the patent owner based on the same art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to In re Recreative Technologies. Examiner should check file history to determine whether the art presented was previously cited/considered ("old art").

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Prior Adverse Office Decisions on Same Art
rubrics_metrics.description: A prior decision adverse to patentability by the Office based upon prior art patents or printed publications would usually mean a substantially new question of patentability is present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An example is a reissue application abandoned after rejection without disclaimer. Examiner should consider such prior adverse determinations when deciding the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Federal Court Decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal court decisions bearing on claim validity affect the SNQ analysis depending on finality and outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A final holding of invalidity/unenforceability by a court (after all appeals) is controlling on the Office and means an SNQ is not present as to those claims. A final holding of validity does not necessarily preclude an SNQ because of different standards of proof; the Office decides independently and may accord deference to district court factual findings. Nonfinal (interlocutory) holdings are not controlling. See In re Swanson, In re Baxter, Ethicon v. Quigg.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner Should Not Reject Claims in the Order for Reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should limit the discussion in the order for reexamination to whether an SNQ has been raised and SHOULD NOT reject claims in the order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any rejection of claims will be made in the first Office action on patentability issued after the expiration of the time for submitting the patent owner statement and requester reply that follow the examiner’s order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Owner Statements Not Considered at Ordering Stage
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner claim scope statement and accompanying information submitted pursuant to 37 CFR 1.501(a)(2) will not be considered by the examiner when making the determination to order reexamination under 35 U.S.C. 304.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C. 301(d) provides that such statements and additional information submitted pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 301(c) are not to be considered by the Office for any purpose other than to determine the proper meaning of a patent claim in an ordered proceeding. These materials will be considered during the examination stage if reexamination is ordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim Construction Standard for Ordering
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining whether to order reexamination, the Office will determine the proper meaning of the patent claims by giving the claims their broadest reasonable interpretation consistent with the specification (In re Yamamoto), except for expired patents where Phillips claim construction applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For expired patents in reexamination, claim construction follows Phillips v. AWH Corp. (ordinary and customary meaning) as applied by the courts. If reexamination is ordered, owner statements and accompanying information will be considered during the examination stage to the fullest extent possible when determining claim scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner Should Indicate Initial Positions on Issues Identified
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should indicate, insofar as possible, his or her initial position on all issues identified in the request so that comment may be received in the patent owner’s statement and the requester’s reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing initial positions facilitates comment and helps frame the subsequent examination stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing and Mailing of Decision
rubrics_metrics.description: After the examiner prepares, proofreads, and signs the decision, the reexamination file and decision are forwarded for clerical processing; a copy is mailed to the patent owner and any third party along with required copies of prior art documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The signed decision and copies of prior art are made of record in the reexamination electronic file. Coordinating is performed by the Central Reexamination Unit (CRU) Legal Instrument Examiner (LIE) and technical support staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination After Reissue of Patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a request for reexamination is filed on a patent after a reissue patent for that patent has already issued, reexamination will be denied because the patent on which the request is based has been surrendered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reexamination of the reissued patent is desired, a new request for reexamination that includes and is based on the specification and claims of the reissue patent must be filed. See MPEP § 2285 for related timing issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Additional Prior Art and Limited Searching
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner is not limited to the patents/publications cited in the request and may perform a limited additional search where there is a reasonable likelihood prior art can be found to supply deficiencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such searching should be limited to areas most likely to contain the deficiency and only when it reasonably may supply necessary prior art to establish an SNQ.

rubrics_metrics.name: SNQ Can Be Presented for Claims Not Requested
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the examiner ordinarily concentrates on claims for which reexamination was requested, the finding of an SNQ can be based upon a claim of the patent other than the ones requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request may seek reexamination of particular claims, but the examiner can determine an SNQ is present as to other claims without finding an SNQ for the requested claims. The decision on the request should discuss all patent claims requested for reexamination.
